skill.name: crawl4ai
skill.description: Guides agents through Crawl4AI web crawling, markdown conversion, structured extraction, batch crawling, and JavaScript-rendered page handling.
skill.summary: Use Crawl4AI to crawl web pages, extract structured data, and convert sites into clean markdown.
skill.author: smallnest

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown documentation, placeholder API-key examples, and code-fence backticks. Confirmed risks are expected crawler side effects: local result writes, Google Search requests, unrestricted user-supplied URLs, and dual-use anti-detection guidance. Static review was capped at 400/959 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 559 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Anti-detection and protected-content examples can be misused.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear authorization requirements and remove guidance that frames proxies or fingerprint changes as ways to bypass site controls.

remediation.issue: Scripts accept arbitrary URLs from command-line and file input.
remediation.suggestion: Validate URL schemes, block localhost and private network ranges by default, and support domain allowlists for agent-driven runs.

remediation.issue: Scripts write outputs to fixed names or caller-provided paths.
remediation.suggestion: Write into a dedicated output directory, refuse path traversal, and warn before overwriting existing files.

remediation.issue: API token examples include local configuration storage guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Document file permission expectations and prefer environment variables or secret managers for shared systems.

content.value_statement: Web pages are hard to convert into clean, reusable data. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use Crawl4AI for crawling, markdown, and extraction workflows.
actual_capabilities: Runs Crawl4AI CLI examples for single-page crawling and markdown output.
Shows Python SDK patterns for AsyncWebCrawler and CrawlerRunConfig.
Supports CSS schema extraction for repeatable structured data tasks.
Provides batch crawling examples for multiple URLs with concurrency settings.
Explains JavaScript waits, sessions, screenshots, proxies, and content filters.
Includes helper scripts for basic crawling, batch crawling, extraction, and Google result parsing.
limitations: Requires Crawl4AI, Playwright browsers, and network access in the local environment.
Some LLM extraction examples require a configured provider API key.
Website selectors can break when target pages change their HTML structure.
Users must confirm they have permission to crawl each target site.

use_cases.title: Convert Documentation Sites
use_cases.description: Turn public documentation pages into clean markdown for analysis, migration, or knowledge base preparation.

use_cases.title: Monitor Product Listings
use_cases.description: Use CSS extraction schemas to collect product names, prices, links, and descriptions from permitted sources.

use_cases.title: Prototype Crawling Pipelines
use_cases.description: Test Crawl4AI CLI and SDK settings before building a larger automated data pipeline.

prompt_templates.title: Crawl One Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner task for a public page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Crawl4AI to crawl this URL and return clean markdown. Confirm the URL before running any command: <url>

prompt_templates.title: Extract Repeating Items
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task with visible repeated page elements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Crawl4AI CSS extraction plan for this page. Extract titles, links, dates, and summaries from repeated items: <url>

prompt_templates.title: Batch Crawl Sources
prompt_templates.scenario: Multi-source research task with controlled concurrency.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Crawl4AI batch crawl for these approved URLs. Save markdown outputs and summarize failed pages: <urls>

prompt_templates.title: Build Extraction Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for repeatable structured extraction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Crawl4AI pipeline that generates a schema once, reuses it without LLM calls, and validates extracted fields for: <task>

output_examples.input: Crawl a public product category page and extract product details.
output_examples.output: A concise extraction plan with selectors, expected fields, output file names, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: Convert a documentation page into markdown.
output: Clean page title and section headings.
Main article content without navigation noise.
A note listing links, images, and crawl warnings.

output_examples.input: Run a batch crawl for approved research sources.
output_examples.output: A progress summary with successful pages, failed pages, saved markdown locations, and retry recommendations.

best_practices: Confirm permission, scope, and rate limits before crawling any site.
Prefer CSS extraction schemas for repeatable pages before using LLM extraction.
Write outputs into a dedicated working directory and review files before reuse.
anti_patterns: Do not crawl authenticated or protected pages without explicit authorization.
Do not use proxy or anti-detection settings to bypass site rules.
Do not store API tokens in shared files or commit generated output.

faq.question: Does this skill perform crawling by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and scripts that call Crawl4AI when the user approves a crawl.

faq.question: Can it handle JavaScript-rendered pages?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use browser waits, page timeouts, and Crawl4AI browser settings for dynamic content.

faq.question: Does it require an LLM API key?
faq.answer: Basic crawling and CSS extraction do not. LLM-based extraction examples require a configured provider key.

faq.question: Can it crawl multiple URLs?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes CLI loops and Python SDK examples for concurrent batch crawling.

faq.question: Where are results saved?
faq.answer: The bundled scripts save markdown, screenshots, and extraction results in local files near the working directory.

faq.question: What should users check before running it?
faq.answer: Users should verify target permissions, expected output paths, rate limits, and any API token requirements.
